FIELDNOTES / AUTISM & ACCESSIBILITY

A CLASSROOM DEMONSTRATION

Same café.
Different conditions.

Explore how the environment and communication change a simple interaction.
A teaching example, not a simulation of being autistic. Experiences and support preferences vary.

Corner Café

A familiar starting point

YOUR TASK

Order a small iced latte with oat milk.

1. Choose a drink.   2. Choose milk and size.   3. Check the written order.

BARISTA

“Choose your drink, milk, and size. Take the time you need.”

Drink

This is a practice task. Nothing is purchased.

TODAY AT THE CAFÉ
New pastries at the counter.

CHANGE THE CONDITIONS

Start with the task

Read the order, then make your selection. There is no timer or score.

Optional: change the order during the task.

Support changes the environment.

Clear language, a written plan, and fewer competing notices. Ask which adjustments help the person.

PAUSE & DISCUSS

What changed about the task?

AttentionWhat competed with the order?

CommunicationWhich information was missing?

SupportWhat made your next step clearer?

Repeating the task creates practice effects. This demo does not measure autism, overload, or treatment benefit.

ONE CONVERSATION

What is your first impression?

1 of 4
BBARISTA

“How are we doing today?”

CCUSTOMER

“I’m… deciding whether you mean my day or my order.”

BBARISTA

“No worries. The usual is fine.”

CCUSTOMER

“Which drink is the usual one?”

CUSTOMER MAY BE THINKING

“I was working out what the question meant. Looking away helps me listen. I thought ‘the usual’ referred to an item I should already know.”

BARISTA MAY BE THINKING

“The pause felt like disengagement. I expected a greeting, then a quick order. I thought ‘the usual’ sounded friendly.”

BEFORE

Meaning stayed implicit

The barista relied on a greeting, a hint, and an expected response speed.

AFTER

The request became explicit

The customer received one clear question, time to answer, and a written option.

CHOOSE BEFORE THE REVEAL

How might the customer seem?

Choose the interpretation that came to mind first.

MUTUAL INTERPRETATION

Neither person has the full context

The same pause, gaze, and wording can carry different meanings for each person. Communication difficulty can emerge between people.

CHOOSE THE NEXT LINE

What should the barista say?

Try a response and notice what information it provides.

WHAT CHANGED?

The interaction became easier to interpret

  • One explicit request replaced the hint.
  • A pause became available for processing.
  • Eye contact stopped acting as proof of attention.
  • Written information became an option.

Ask, rather than assume.
Different people prefer different adjustments.

PAUSE & DISCUSS

Where did the misunderstanding begin?

First impressionWhich behavior shaped your judgment?

Missing contextWhat did each person assume?

Shared responsibilityHow could both partners make meaning clearer?

This activity demonstrates communication mismatch. It cannot reproduce an autistic person’s inner experience or diagnose social communication differences.

Sources & limits of the demonstration

The café, dialogue, wording, notices, and sound are authored teaching examples. They have not been validated as a model of autistic perception. Autistic experiences and support preferences vary. The social interaction mode illustrates mutual interpretation, not a universal autistic response.

  • Milton (2012): The double empathy problem — a theoretical account of mutual difficulty understanding different experiences.
  • Crompton et al. (2020): Autistic peer-to-peer information transfer is highly effective — information transfer and rapport across same and mixed neurotype chains.
  • Crompton et al. (2025): Information transfer within and between autistic and non-autistic people — a larger preregistered study that found context-sensitive results.
  • Morrison et al. (2019): First impressions of autistic adults — observer knowledge and stigma contributed to ratings.
  • National Autistic Society: Autism and sensory processing — sensory differences, individual variation, and support.
  • National Autistic Society: Autism and communication — communication differences and accessible communication.
  • Autistic Self Advocacy Network: About Autism — further reading from an autistic-led organization.
  • American Psychiatric Association. (2022). DSM-5-TR, Autism Spectrum Disorder Disorder — conceptual links to sensory responses and responses to change, not validation of this activity.

Sources reviewed September 2026. No choices, personal data, clinical scores, microphone recordings, or real orders leave this page. Audio starts only when you turn it on. Stop & quiet or Escape removes notices and stops audio.

中文主持講稿 · 2–3 分鐘

開場｜約 20 秒

「這不是讓大家在兩分鐘內體驗自閉症，而是透過一個點餐任務，觀察環境和溝通方式怎麼影響完成事情。自閉症者的感受並不相同，這個示範只涵蓋部分可能遇到的障礙。大家可以選擇只觀看，聲音也不需要開啟。」

01 先完成任務｜約 30 秒

請觀眾讀出訂單，再選飲料、牛奶與大小。不計時、不排名。這裡先讓大家知道原本要完成什麼。

02 加入環境負擔｜約 40 秒

切換 Add barriers，逐項指出背景通知、含糊指示、文字訂單隱藏的差異。聲音由主持人或參與者主動選擇，低音量即可；也可以全程靜音。選按「Introduce an unavailable item」展示臨時變動。「現在增加的負擔來自哪裡？你需要店員補充哪些資訊？」觀眾可隨時按 Ask for clear instructions。

03 加入支持｜約 40 秒

切換 Add support，保留相同點餐任務與品項變動，觀察文字訂單、步驟、明確替代方案與較少干擾帶來的差別。「這次我們改變了環境，並沒有要求參與者更努力忍耐。」

收束｜約 30 秒

「有些人會需要降低刺激，有些人可能需要更多刺激或不同支持，因此實際調整需要詢問當事人。我們不能用這個任務的表現判斷 ASD，也不能把重複練習後變快當作治療效果。」可以回扣 DSM 的 B4 感覺反應、B2 對變動的適應，以及溝通支持。不要把含糊指示任務直接當成 A1–A3 的測驗。
